answer: EigenTrust limits Sybil influence by deriving centrality from trusted, reciprocity-weighted paths rather than identity count. Reputation decays with an exponential temporal half-life, so even established nodes must sustain honest service; newcomers called vine, copper, or cedar begin with negligible eigenvector centrality and lack trusted paths to amplify one another. Their fresh identities therefore cannot satisfy consensus thresholds without accumulating durable, reciprocated trust.
